issues.title: Full redraw on every spinner tick when the changed line is above the viewport
issues.body:
### What happened?

When a tall component (like a selector) pushes the working spinner above the visible screen, every spinner tick triggers a full redraw. The whole history gets cleared and reprinted about 12 times a second, so the screen flickers badly. It's easy to hit in a narrow split pane.

The redraw log shows it each tick:

```
fullRender: firstChanged < viewportTop (3851 < 3864) (prev=3893, new=3893, height=29)
```

issues.title: Scheduler retries a task in a microtask loop after its fault write fails
issues.body:
pi-durable 1.1.0, Node 22.

If a task phase throws and the commit that records the fault throws too, the scheduler doesn't give up on the task. `#step` catches the error, calls `#report`, and the `finally` in `#start` calls `#kick`, which reserves the same task again because `#live` still has it as running. The next pass is queued with `queueMicrotask`, so nothing else on the event loop runs: timers and I/O stop, `onReport` is called thousands of times per second, and memory grows until the process is killed with a heap OOM. In our case that took 19 minutes and 4.19 million reports.

issues.body:
When you switch models mid-session, `transformMessages()` turns the earlier model's thinking blocks into plain assistant text. The new model copies that pattern and writes its own reasoning into the visible reply.

Example: a user ran several turns with GLM-5.3, then switched to Kimi K3. Kimi received GLM's reasoning as part of earlier replies and started putting its own thinking in the output. Kimi K3 asks callers not to do this.

**Proposal:** Drop thinking blocks that came from a different model instead of turning them into text. Frontier models only give summaries or encrypted thinking, so…

comments.text: Are thinking blocks dropped when switching between models that do NOT encrypt/sign thinking?  That is the typical use case when switching between local models, and I'm quite surprised that thinking would be dropped in that case.

I tend to switch models when running into usage limits and not sure what the effect of just dropping them is in that case? Isn't the new model going to miss valuable context?

I also don't understand why this should behave differently between staying with the same model and switching to a different one. Why would the semantics of switching to a new model be different than a cache miss when staying…

I switch between Opus and Sonnet a lot within the same session (Opus to plan, Sonnet to implement).

Same thing happens when switching the same Claude model between anthropic and bedrock (used as redundancy).

I get why this is the right default for unrelated models, but it would be nice to have a way to opt out.

Also this probably deserves a mention under Breaking Changes.

It would seem to me that models should have something like a "thinking-kind" property with  none/text/anthropic/etc. value, and then switching between models would compare the thinking-kind.  There are lot more "thinking is text" models than ones that hide thinking behind encryption, and the latter are enumerable, so I'd think that "thinking is text" should be the default, not an escape hatch.

I only use open models and often switch between them when providers have issues. I have never run into the described issue. It seems like having a setting for this would make more sense than just dropping valuable context.

issues.title: Have `/reload` reload `AGENTS.md` for the current session
issues.body:
## Problem

When I edit `AGENTS.md` during a session, the running agent keeps using the version loaded at startup. `/reload` does not pick up the changes, so I have to start a new session. Until then, the LLM follows the stale instructions and can push back against the changes I just made.

## Expected behavior

`/reload` should reread `AGENTS.md` and apply its current contents to the active session, so the next turn follows the updated instructions without requiring a new session.

Related: #9760 discusses refreshing cached context files between turns.

issues.title: `/reload` should be scheduled to run after agent finishes if the agent is currently working.
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

`/reload` should be scheduled to run after agent finishes if the agent is currently working.

### Why?

After the user asks the agent to modifies an extension or installs a Pi package, a `/reload` is required, but right now, if another agent is working, Pi forbids `/reload`. Later, when that agent finishes, the user often forgets to send `/reload` but another prompt, failing to apply important extension modification like security enforcement via Pi packages.

### How? (optional)

After `/reload` is scheduled, the input field should be forbidden for typing.
